title: Compact connection orchestrator and adaptive retry builder for SDK ergonomics
author: Priya Raman
description:
Motivation: Teams repeatedly ask for smaller cognitive-surface SDKs that still offer production-quality connection pooling, resilient retries, and minimal per-language boilerplate. This PR introduces a Compact Connection Orchestrator (CCO) and an Adaptive Retry Builder (ARB) surfaced as light ergonomic shims in the Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. The goal is to provide a single, documented pattern for: (1) shared connection pooling across streaming and unary flows, (2) adaptive per-request retry policies that can be tuned per-model/route, and (3) a lazy auth adapter that prefetches credentials just-in-time to reduce cold-start auth latency while avoiding credential overfetch in high-concurrency apps.

What changed:
- Core: new compact/conn/orchestrator module that centralizes socket/http2/ws pool management and exposes a minimal lifecycle API: start(), borrow(), return(), drain(). Pools are short-lived by default but can be pinned by higher-level SDKs for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Retry: adaptive/retry/builder implements sample-windowed backoff adjustments. ARB monitors transient error rates and average token latency to automatically scale between three preset profiles (fast, balanced, conservative). Developers can still provide static RetryPolicy objects.
- Auth: auth/lazy_adapter defers credential fetch until the first borrow() for a connection and attaches a lightweight lease that heartbeat-refreshes only when streaming or long-lived connections are observed.
- Streaming ergonomic facades: the SDK stream client now exposes a Pause/Resume hook and a heartbeat callback for reconnect hints; streaming consumers can opt into bufferless line-mode or chunked-accumulate mode.
- Cross-language: small per-language shims implemented for ergonomics and naming conventions; no API breaking changes to existing top-level client constructors. Each SDK bumped: Python -> 1.12.0, TypeScript -> 2.5.0, Go -> 1.4.3.

Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves previous semantics: existing clients that do not opt into the orchestrator continue using the prior per-request connection behavior. To opt in, set client.opts.connectionOrchestrator = {enabled: true, pinPool: false} or call RedwoodConnection.orchestrate() when bootstrapping.

Performance and telemetry: added telemetry hooks for pool utilization, borrow latency, retry-profile-switch events, and auth-lease heartbeats. These are emitted to existing SDK telemetry endpoints and surfaced in Console under the new "SDK connection" dashboard.

Testing and CI: unit tests cover pool lifecycle, borrow/return racing, adaptive window transitions, and lazy auth expiry. Integration tests validate streaming resume semantics with simulated auth rotation and HA proxy failover.

Migration: documented migration guide with step-by-step opt-in examples and a short checklist for Dedicated/Private customers (KMS/HSM considerations).

Rollout: feature flags enabled on staging for 48h smoke; rolled to main and tagged for GA.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc and benchmarks attached
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Telemetry and Dashboard changes
- [x] Cross-SDK examples updated
- [x] Release notes prepared
